newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Post-handover jitters hit Hong Kong prison inmates.
newsitem.headline: Post-handover jitters hit Hong Kong prison inmates.

text.p: Human rights watchdogs said on Friday inmates in Hong Kong prisons were worried for their future after the territory reverts to China at midnight on June 30.

"Given China's notoriously poor prison conditions and its frequent use of capital punishment, it is unsurprising that some Hong Kong prisoners have expressed grave apprehensions regarding their treatment under Chinese rule," Human Rights Watch/Asia and Hong Kong Human Rights Monitor said in a joint statement.
Both agencies urged future monitoring of prison conditions to allay fears of inmates and also drew attention to their present conditions.
"Overcrowding, which is a problem now and, according to official estimates, will continue to be a problem for the foreseeable future," the statement said.
The agencies also urged authorities to allow prisoners out of their day rooms more frequently and to give more work, recreational and educational opportunities.
Beijing Justice Minister Xiao Yang in February dismissed foreign criticism of China's jails, saying they aimed to combine punishment with reform and to mix labour with education.
